findings.issue: The start screen's Learn link points at https://github.com/Nihalpi1212/claude/tree/HEAD/pigment/docs/user. GitHub resolves HEAD to the repository's default branch, which is claude/fervent-newton-263lz3 (the JavaScript app; `git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD`), and pigment/docs/user does not exist there, so the link is a 404. Even on the Pigment branch the guide it opens is PhotoCraft's, unchanged: its landing page is titled PhotoCraft, says 'Ask in Discord (discord.gg/artcraft) or open an issue in the issue tracker (github.com/storytold/photocraft/issues). In PhotoCraft, Help > Report an Issue opens the same issue tracker' (false in Pigment), and 'Install PhotoCraft' sends the person to getartcraft.com, the ArtCraft Launcher and storytold/photocraft/releases/latest. 20 pages under docs/user name PhotoCraft/ArtCraft and 27 lines link storytold, getartcraft or Discord. The rebrand check cannot catch it: pigment-rebrand.py skips every .md under docs/. The same default-branch problem makes 'Pigment on GitHub' (links.rs GITHUB, start-screen 'GitHub') and the AppStream homepage/help URLs open the JavaScript app's tree and README.
findings.scenario: Install 0.5.0, start Pigment, click Learn on the start screen: the browser shows GitHub's 404. After the branch is merged to the default branch (or with the link fixed to the branch), Learn opens a guide that tells the person to report bugs to PhotoCraft's tracker and Discord and to install PhotoCraft from getartcraft.com or update it with the ArtCraft Launcher.
findings.test: A unit test in links.rs that every Pigment link names a ref that exists for the release (e.g. asserts TUTORIALS contains `/tree/pigment-v{brand::VERSION}/` rather than `/tree/HEAD/`); a CI step (or an extension of pigment-rebrand.py --check) that greps pigment/docs/user for storytold/photocraft, getartcraft, discord.gg and fails. Manually: `curl -sI https://github.com/Nihalpi1212/claude/tree/HEAD/pigment/docs/user` returns 404 today.
findings.fix: Point TUTORIALS at the release tag, built from the version: format!("https://github.com/Nihalpi1212/claude/tree/pigment-v{}/pigment/docs/user", brand::VERSION) (it can't be a const then; or point it at the release branch). Do the same for GITHUB (`.../tree/pigment-v<ver>/pigment`) and the metainfo homepage/help URLs, or make claude/pigment-photocraft the default branch. Rebrand docs/user before the tag: index.md, getting-started/install.md (Pigment's release assets and file names, no launcher), the 'Get help'/'Still stuck?' sections (Pigment's issues, no Discord), and add docs/user to the rebrand check (allow only the upstream credit).

findings.where: pigment/crates/automation/src/app_dirs.rs:48 (resolve reads PHOTOCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR, used by the app and pigment-cli); apps/photocraft/src/single_instance.rs:314-346 (instance.lock / instance.json in that folder); PHOTOCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT / PHOTOCRAFT_CONTROL_TOKEN_FILE in apps/photocraft/src/launch_args.rs and pigment-cli mcp --bridge
findings.issue: Pigment reads PhotoCraft's own environment variables. A person who set PHOTOCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR for an installed PhotoCraft (the documented way to move its settings) gets Pigment and PhotoCraft sharing one settings folder: preferences.json, ui.ron, logs, Recovery, agent-connection.json, the agent token and the single-instance lock. Because both programs use instance.lock/instance.json there, starting Pigment (or double-clicking a .pigment file) while PhotoCraft runs finds the lock taken and hands the files to PhotoCraft's window; Pigment never opens. Likewise PHOTOCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT set for PhotoCraft makes `pigment --control`/`pigment-cli mcp` use PhotoCraft's port and token file. This breaks the rule that nothing is shared with an installed PhotoCraft.
findings.scenario: Windows: setx PHOTOCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR D:\PhotoCraftSettings, PhotoCraft running. Install Pigment 0.5.0 MSI, double-click poster.pigment: the file opens as a tab in PhotoCraft (or PhotoCraft's settings and recovery files are rewritten by Pigment when PhotoCraft is closed).
findings.test: In crates/automation/src/app_dirs.rs tests: resolve(env with PHOTOCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR=/x only) must return the platform Pigment folder; with PIGMENT_CONFIG_DIR=/y it returns /y.
findings.fix: Read PIGMENT_CONFIG_DIR (and PIGMENT_CONTROL_PORT, PIGMENT_CONTROL_TOKEN*) in the shipped binaries and ignore the PHOTOCRAFT_* names for anything that selects a folder, port or token; keep PHOTOCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR only as a test hook if the tests need it (e.g. accepted only when PIGMENT_CONFIG_DIR is unset and a test-only cfg is on), and update the CLI tests that set it. List the new names in FORK.md.

findings.issue: The version job publishes every 0.x version as a GitHub pre-release. Pigment 0.4.0 (the JavaScript app, tag pigment-v0.4.0) was published as a full release by the old workflow, so after 0.5.0 is published GitHub's 'Latest' release, /releases/latest and the repository sidebar keep pointing at the JavaScript 0.4.0 that 0.5.0 replaces, and 0.5.0 carries a 'Pre-release' badge although the README and release notes present it as the version that replaces 0.4.
findings.scenario: Dispatch the release with tag pigment-v0.5.0. Open https://github.com/Nihalpi1212/claude/releases/latest: it shows Pigment 0.4.0 (Electron). Anyone following a 'latest release' link or script downloads the old app.
findings.test: After a dry run against a fork: `gh release view --json isPrerelease,isLatest pigment-v0.5.0`; or a check in the version job that echoes prerelease=false for 0.5.0.
findings.fix: If 0.5.0 is meant to be Pigment's current release (the release notes say so), drop the `0.*` rule (prerelease only for a `-suffix` version) and pass `make_latest: true` to action-gh-release when prerelease is false. If staying a pre-release is a deliberate choice, say so in the release notes and README ('0.4.0 stays marked Latest until ...').
